extracted.intended_audience: US Government officials and other users of The World Factbook (researchers, educators, general public)
extracted.subtask_description: Official publication, style, data, and usage policies for the CIA's The World Factbook, including coverage, naming/spelling conventions, data sourcing, update and review practices, accessibility, and reuse rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intended audience and tailoring
rubrics_metrics.description: The World Factbook is prepared by the Central Intelligence Agency for the use of US Government officials, and the style, format, coverage, and content are designed to meet their specific requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content and presentation are chosen to satisfy US government information needs; other users should note the government-focused orientation and tailored format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Currency cutoff for edition
rubrics_metrics.description: In general, information available as of 1 January, 2004 was used in the preparation of this edition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the 'last updated' date on pages; the Factbook indicates which snapshot date the edition reflects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authoritative source contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Information is provided by Antarctic Information Program (NSF), Bureau of the Census, Bureau of Labor Statistics, CIA, Defense Intelligence Agency, Department of State, National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency, US Board on Geographic Names, and other public and private sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Factbook aggregates data from multiple government and other sources; specific fields draw from different authoritative agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public-domain status and reuse
rubrics_metrics.description: The Factbook is in the public domain. Accordingly, it may be copied freely without permission of the Central Intelligence Agency (CIA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users may reuse content freely but should cite The World Factbook as a courtesy; consult legal counsel if unsure about a particular intended use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on use of CIA seal
rubrics_metrics.description: The official seal of the CIA, however, may NOT be copied without permission as required by the CIA Act of 1949 (50 U.S.C. section 403m). Misuse of the official seal of the CIA could result in civil and criminal penalties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reusing Factbook content, explicitly avoid reproducing the CIA seal or using imagery that implies CIA endorsement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial review standard
rubrics_metrics.description: At least two Factbook staffers review every item.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates a minimum internal quality-control/review process; users can expect items to have had at least two staff reviews though staff cannot reply to all correspondence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on providing additional data
rubrics_metrics.description: The staff cannot provide data beyond what appears in The World Factbook. The format and information in the Factbook are tailored to the specific requirements of US Government officials and content is focused on their current and anticipated needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for additional or non-public data will not be fulfilled; suggestions for new entries are welcome but the staff will not supply off-record information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Update frequency policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Formerly our Web site (and the published Factbook) were only updated annually. Beginning in November 2001 we instituted a new system of more frequent online updates. The annual printed version of the Factbook is usually released about midyear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Online content may be updated more frequently than print; check online for the most current data and printed edition release timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope: national-level coverage only
rubrics_metrics.description: The World Factbook provides national-level information on countries, territories, and dependencies, but not subnational administrative units within a country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State/province/county-level information is generally not included; cross-reference lists may include major geographic features but not full subnational gazetteer entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entity inclusion and presentation policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Inclusion and ordering of entities (e.g., Taiwan, European Union, Holy See, West Bank/Gaza) follow US Government recognition, BGN recommendations, and practical editorial decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Factbook reflects US Government positions and BGN guidance on naming and inclusion; special cases are explained in notes (e.g., Taiwan listed after regular entries; EU included though not a country).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mapping and territorial depiction policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Territorial occupations/annexations not recognized by the United States Government are not shown on US Government maps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maps and territorial attributions reflect U.S. recognition and BGN decisions; disputed areas may be handled with notes or separate entries rather than shown as part of a claimant state.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naming and spelling conventions (chiefs of state / keyboard)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Factbook staff applies the names and spellings from the Chiefs of State link on the CIA Web site. The World Factbook is prepared using the standard American English computer keyboard and does not use any special characters, symbols, or most diacritical markings in its spellings. Surnames are always spelled with capital letters; they may appear first in some cultures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect anglicized spellings, no diacritics, and surname capitalization conventions; changes or variants may be noted where BGN updates are pending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic naming authority (BGN)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Factbook staff follows the guidance of the United States Board on Geographic Names (BGN). The BGN is the component of the US Government that develops policies, principles, and procedures governing the spelling, use, and application of geographic names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BGN determinations drive geographic naming and spelling in the Factbook; notes are usually included when changes have occurred but are not yet BGN-approved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pronunciation policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The World Factbook does not include pronunciations of country or leader names because of too many variations in pronunciation among English-speaking countries; American English pronunciations are included for some countries like Qatar and Kiribati.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not expect systematic pronunciation guides; a few selected pronunciations may be provided for names where American English guidance is helpful.

rubrics_metrics.name: American vs British spelling policy
rubrics_metrics.description: When American and British spellings of common English words differ, The World Factbook always uses the American spelling, even when these common words form part of a proper name in British English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All common-word spellings follow American conventions regardless of local or British usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source selection principle
rubrics_metrics.description: The Factbook staff uses many different sources to publish what we judge are the most reliable and consistent data for any particular category. Space considerations preclude a listing of these various sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data choices are made based on staff judgment of reliability and consistency; users should consult Notes and Definitions for methodology where available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temperature extremes inclusion rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: The Factbook staff judges that minimum and maximum temperature extremes would only be useful for some (generally smaller) countries. Larger countries can have large temperature extremes that do not represent the landmass as a whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Temperature extremes are generally excluded from standard country entries; the Factbook may adopt such a category in the future with both extremes and typical ranges if warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metric units usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Most of the statistical information in the Factbook is given in metric units, rather than the units standard to US measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of SI/metric units complies with the Metric Conversion Act of 1975 and Executive Order 12770; expect metric presentation for most statistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: GDP methodology (PPP basis)
rubrics_metrics.description: GDP dollar estimates in The World Factbook are derived from purchasing power parity (PPP) calculations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GDP figures may differ from other sources that use nominal exchange rates; see the Notes and Definitions section on GDP methodology for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Percentage distribution rounding policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Some percentage distributions do not add to 100. Because of rounding, percentage distributions do not always add precisely to 100%. We do not force the numbers to add exactly to 100, because doing so would introduce additional error into the distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rounded percentages are presented as computed; users should not assume a forced reconciliation to 100% and should consult original data if exact totals are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numeric rounding convention
rubrics_metrics.description: In deciding on the number of digits to present, the Factbook staff assesses the accuracy of the original data and the needs of US Government officials. The economic data presented follow the rounding convention used by virtually all numerical software applications, namely, any digit followed by a '5' is rounded up to the next higher digit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard computer rounding is used (e.g., 2.5 rounds to 3); rounding decisions balance source accuracy and user needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility and Section 508 compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: The World Factbook home page has a link entitled 'Text/Low Bandwidth Version.' The country data in the text version is fully accessible. We believe The World Factbook is compliant with the Section 508 law in both fact and spirit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the text/low-bandwidth version for better assistive-technology access; report specific accessibility issues via the comment form with details of assistive software/hardware used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official site authenticity
rubrics_metrics.description: Hundreds of 'Factbook' look-alikes exist on the Internet. The Factbook site at: www.cia.gov is the only official site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify that you are using the official CIA-hosted Factbook to ensure authoritative and up-to-date content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Machine-readable and data download availability
rubrics_metrics.description: The Factbook Web site features 'Rank Order' pages for selected Factbook entries and all of the 'Rank Order' pages can be downloaded as tab-delimited data files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fields with a small bar chart icon have rank-order pages available; these can be downloaded for spreadsheet/database use.
